name: 19 · Connectors and signposting for SOC presentations · Natural English
description: 100 microescenarios revisados para practicar conectores naturales y signposting al hablar con clientes y presentar información SOC. Las respuestas dependen de gramática, naturalidad, claridad, organización del discurso y tono profesional; el contexto técnico funciona únicamente como escenario.

questions.question: You are opening a monthly SOC service review. Which sentence sounds most natural and professional?
options: Thanks for your joining. I would start by a brief overview of this month's activity.
Thank you to join. First of all, an overview will be started about this month.
Thanks for joining. I like to start with a brief overview about this month's activity.
Thanks for joining. I'd like to start with a brief overview of this month's activity.
questions.explanation: «I'd like to start with...» es una apertura cortés y natural. Se dice «overview of», no «overview about», y «thanks for joining» evita construcciones poco idiomáticas.
questions.translation: Gracias por asistir. Me gustaría empezar con un breve resumen de la actividad de este mes.

questions.question: Complete the agenda preview: 'I'll begin with the incident summary, ___ the monitoring update, and finish with next steps.'
options: then move on to
afterwards moving to
following with
then I will pass on
questions.explanation: «Then move on to» presenta el siguiente bloque con claridad y mantiene la estructura paralela de la agenda. Las otras opciones no encajan de forma natural en la oración.
questions.translation: Empezaré con el resumen de incidentes, después pasaré a la actualización de monitorización y terminaré con los próximos pasos.

questions.question: The customer is new to the service. Choose the clearest way to provide context before showing charts.
options: Before we get into the figures, let me briefly explain how the service is structured.
Before to see the figures, let me briefly explain how the service has structure.
Before entering into the figures, let me explain briefly how is structured the service.
Previous to getting into figures, I explain how the service structures itself.
questions.explanation: «Before we get into...» y «let me briefly explain...» son fórmulas naturales al hablar. La interrogativa indirecta conserva el orden «how the service is structured».
questions.translation: Antes de entrar en las cifras, permítanme explicar brevemente cómo está estructurado el servicio.

questions.question: Which objective statement works best at the start of a customer briefing?
options: Today's session has as aim to review what changed and agreeing about next steps.
The objective for today consists to review changes and agree about the following steps.
The aim of today's session is reviewing what changed and to agree the next steps.
The aim of today's session is to review what changed and agree on the next steps.
questions.explanation: Tras «the aim ... is» resulta natural usar dos infinitivos paralelos: «to review» y «agree». La colocación correcta es «agree on the next steps».
questions.translation: El objetivo de la sesión de hoy es revisar qué ha cambiado y acordar los próximos pasos.

questions.question: You want to give the audience the background to an investigation. Which signpost sounds natural?
options: To set the scene, the activity began with a small number of unusual sign-ins.
For setting the scene, the activity was beginning by a small number of unusual sign-ins.
For locating us in context, unusual sign-ins were the beginning of the activity.
To put the scenario, the activity started from a little quantity of unusual sign-ins.
questions.explanation: «To set the scene» es una expresión idiomática para introducir contexto. «A small number of» es natural con sustantivos contables como «sign-ins».
questions.translation: Para situarnos, la actividad comenzó con un pequeño número de inicios de sesión inusuales.

questions.question: A slide contains four sections. How would you introduce them without sounding overly formal?
options: Here are the matters which I pretend to cover today: trends, actions, changes, and priorities.
These are the themes I have intention for covering today: trends, actions, changes, and priorities.
The following points are those that will be covered by myself in today's date.
Here's what I'd like to cover today: trends, open actions, service changes, and priorities.
questions.explanation: «Here's what I'd like to cover» es directo, cortés y propio del inglés hablado profesional. «Pretend» no significa «pretender» en este contexto y las demás opciones son recargadas.
questions.translation: Esto es lo que me gustaría tratar hoy: tendencias, acciones abiertas, cambios en el servicio y prioridades.

questions.question: Choose the most natural promise of value to the audience.
options: By ending the session, a clear view about the current position and necessary decisions will be had.
For the session's end, you will dispose of a clear view of the position and decisions that we need to take.
At the end of the session, you will be having a clear vision about the actual position and needed decisions.
By the end of the session, you'll have a clear view of the current position and the decisions we need to make.
questions.explanation: «By the end of the session, you'll have...» comunica el resultado esperado de forma natural. «Current» significa «actual» y «a clear view of» es la colocación adecuada.
questions.translation: Al final de la sesión, tendrán una visión clara de la situación actual y de las decisiones que necesitamos.

questions.question: You are about to present a colleague who will cover threat trends. Which introduction sounds best?
options: Before we begin, let me briefly introduce Sam, who'll take us through the threat trends later.
Previously to begin, I want to introduce to Sam, that later will pass us through the trends.
Before beginning, let me present briefly Sam, who will explain us the threat trends later.
Before we start, let me make a brief presentation of Sam, who'll expose the threat trends.
questions.explanation: Se usa «introduce Sam» sin «to» y «take us through» significa explicar algo paso a paso. «Explain us» y «expose the trends» no son naturales aquí.
questions.translation: Antes de empezar, permítanme presentar brevemente a Sam, que más tarde nos explicará las tendencias de amenazas.

questions.question: Which version introduces a three-part agenda most clearly?
options: We have three items in the agenda: performance, recent cases, and improvements planned.
We have three items on the agenda: performance, recent cases, and planned improvements.
There are three points over today's agenda, being performance, cases, and planned improvements.
The agenda is composed by three items: performance, recent cases, and improvements.
questions.explanation: La colocación estándar es «on the agenda». La enumeración breve y paralela ayuda a la audiencia a anticipar la estructura.
questions.translation: Tenemos tres puntos en el orden del día: rendimiento, casos recientes y mejoras previstas.

questions.question: The room is ready and you want to begin collaboratively. What would you say?
options: Do we start with a quick look to the general picture?
Shall we start with a quick look at the overall picture?
Are we starting by having a quick vision of the overall picture?
Shall we begin for seeing quickly the picture in general?
questions.explanation: «Shall we start with...?» es una invitación natural y colaborativa. Se dice «a look at» y «the overall picture».
questions.translation: ¿Empezamos con un vistazo rápido a la situación general?

questions.question: You have finished the executive summary and want to introduce service performance. Choose the smoothest transition.
options: Being the headline results covered, now we pass to see service performance deeply.
Now after covering headlines, it corresponds to look about performance in detail.
Now that we covered the headline results, let's look service performance with more detail.
Now that we've covered the headline results, let's look at service performance in more detail.
questions.explanation: «Now that we've covered...» conecta lo anterior con lo siguiente, y «look at ... in more detail» es la combinación idiomática.
questions.translation: Ahora que hemos visto los resultados principales, analicemos con más detalle el rendimiento del servicio.

questions.question: Complete the transition: 'We've discussed alert volumes. ___ how the team handled the most significant cases.'
options: We are passing now at
Let's change now into
Let's turn now to
Let's go ahead about
questions.explanation: «Let's turn now to...» es una señal clara y natural para cambiar de sección en una presentación.
questions.translation: Hemos hablado del volumen de alertas. Pasemos ahora a cómo gestionó el equipo los casos más relevantes.

questions.question: A presenter needs to link the discussion of risk to a slide on recommendations. Which phrase fits best?
options: With this we are arriving at recommendations facing the next quarter.
This brings to us the recommendations for the following trimester.
This carries us until the recommendations of the next quarter.
This brings us to the recommendations for the next quarter.
questions.explanation: «This brings us to...» enlaza lógicamente una sección con la siguiente. «Recommendations for» es más natural que traducciones literales con «of» o «facing».
questions.translation: Esto nos lleva a las recomendaciones para el próximo trimestre.

questions.question: Which sentence moves to a new topic while acknowledging the change?
options: Moving to another theme, I would like discussing about the reporting schedule.
Passing to a distinct topic, I like to discuss over the schedule of reports.
Changing of matter, the reporting schedule is what I would want to discuss.
Moving on to a different topic, I'd like to discuss the reporting schedule.
questions.explanation: «Moving on to a different topic» señala el cambio con suavidad. «Discuss» no lleva «about» y suele ir seguido directamente del objeto.
questions.translation: Pasando a otro tema, me gustaría hablar del calendario de informes.

questions.question: You need to explain one prerequisite before presenting the dashboard. Which order marker is clearest?
options: Before that we look at the dashboard, there is a definition for clarifying.
Before we look at the dashboard, there is one definition we need to clarify.
Previous to see the dashboard, one definition needs that we clarify it.
Before looking the dashboard, there is one definition that we need clarify.
questions.explanation: «Before we look at...» anticipa un paso previo. «Look at» y «need to clarify» son las estructuras correctas.
questions.translation: Antes de ver el panel, hay una definición que debemos aclarar.

questions.question: Select the natural sequence for describing a review process.
options: At first, information is validated; posteriorly, context is assessed; finally comes agreeing about action.
Firstly we validate, in second we assess, and in final we are agreeing the action.
First, we validate the information; next, we assess the context; finally, we agree on the action.
In first place, we validate information; after, we value the context; at last, we accord the action.
questions.explanation: «First, next, finally» crea una secuencia clara y equilibrada. También son naturales «assess the context» y «agree on the action».
questions.translation: Primero validamos la información; después evaluamos el contexto; por último acordamos la acción.

questions.question: The data quality section is complete. Choose the best sentence to introduce conclusions based on it.
options: After having the data quality reviewed, we can consider what are telling us the figures.
Having reviewed about the data quality, now we can consider what tell us the figures.
Once reviewed data quality, we are now able for considering what the figures say us.
Having reviewed the data quality, we can now consider what the figures tell us.
questions.explanation: «Having reviewed...» indica que una fase ya terminó antes de la siguiente. La interrogativa indirecta mantiene «what the figures tell us».
questions.translation: Tras revisar la calidad de los datos, ya podemos considerar qué nos indican las cifras.

questions.question: During a live briefing, you need to pause the planned flow for an urgent update. What sounds most professional?
options: Before continuing, I want to attend briefly the update arrived this morning.
Prior to continue, let me deal shortly about this morning's arrived update.
Before we follow, I would like addressing the update which entered this morning.
Before we continue, I'd like to briefly address the update that came in this morning.
questions.explanation: «Before we continue...» marca una pausa clara. «Address the update» y «came in this morning» son expresiones naturales en un contexto profesional.
questions.translation: Antes de continuar, me gustaría comentar brevemente la actualización que llegó esta mañana.

questions.question: Which transition signals that the presentation has reached a decision point?
options: At this moment of the presentation, it is needed to decide what action goes firstly.
At this point, we need to decide which action should come first.
On this point, we must take a decision about which action comes in first place.
In this point, we need deciding which action should come the first.
questions.explanation: «At this point» sitúa a la audiencia en la estructura. «Decide which...» es directo; «take a decision» es posible en algunos dialectos, pero «make a decision» sería más natural.
questions.translation: Llegados a este punto, debemos decidir qué acción debe ir primero.

questions.question: You want to introduce the next issue without using 'next' twice. Choose the best wording.
options: The following point I'd like to address is the handover between teams.
The following point I'd like to address about is the handover among teams.
The point that follows and I like to treat is the handover between teams.
The next following issue to be attended by me concerns about team handover.
questions.explanation: «The following point I'd like to address is...» evita la repetición y suena natural. «Address» no necesita «about».
questions.translation: El siguiente punto que me gustaría abordar es el traspaso entre equipos.

questions.question: A second benefit supports your recommendation. Choose the most natural addition.
options: Additionally to this, the new format does the weekly update easier for scanning.
In addition, the new format makes the weekly update easier to scan.
In addition to, the new format makes easier to scan the weekly update.
As an addition, the weekly update results more easy to scan in the new format.
questions.explanation: «In addition,» funciona como conector independiente. La estructura natural es «make + object + adjective»: «makes the update easier».
questions.translation: Además, el nuevo formato hace que la actualización semanal sea más fácil de revisar rápidamente.

questions.question: You want to add a related observation during a customer call. What would you say?
options: One more point worthy of mention about is the stability of response times.
Another point worth mentioning is that response times remained stable.
Another point worth to mention is that the response times kept stable.
Other point that deserves mentioning it is response times remained stables.
questions.explanation: La expresión fija es «worth mentioning», sin «to». «Remained stable» es una combinación natural y concisa.
questions.translation: Otro punto que merece la pena mencionar es que los tiempos de respuesta se mantuvieron estables.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: '___ improving clarity, the revised report reduces unnecessary detail.'
options: In addition of
As well
As well as
Besides of
questions.explanation: «As well as» puede ir seguido de gerundio: «as well as improving». «Besides of» e «in addition of» no son construcciones correctas.
questions.translation: Además de mejorar la claridad, el informe revisado reduce los detalles innecesarios.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a balanced structure to reinforce two benefits?
options: The change not only shortens the report but makes also the conclusions more clear.
The change both not only shortens the report and also clarifies more the conclusions.
The change not only shortens the report but also makes the conclusions clearer.
Not only the change shortens the report, but also it makes clearer the conclusions.
questions.explanation: La pareja «not only ... but also ...» exige estructuras paralelas. «Shortens» y «makes» quedan correctamente equilibrados.
questions.translation: El cambio no solo acorta el informe, sino que también hace más claras las conclusiones.

questions.question: The audience already knows about one delay; you need to add another factor without sounding dramatic. Choose the best option.
options: Also there is a dependency of the process of approval from the customer.
There is as well a dependence with the customer's process for approving.
Too, the customer's approval process supposes one dependency.
There is also a dependency on the customer's approval process.
questions.explanation: «There is also...» añade información de forma neutral. La colocación habitual es «a dependency on».
questions.translation: También existe una dependencia del proceso de aprobación del cliente.

questions.question: Choose the spoken signpost that adds a particularly useful detail.
options: Even more, that same view can use itself during the weekly call.
What's more, the same view can be used in the weekly call.
What's moreover, the same view is usable in the call of every week.
What is more important, the same view can be used on the call weekly.
questions.explanation: «What's more,» añade y refuerza una idea en inglés hablado profesional. No debe confundirse con «what is more important», que cambia el significado.
questions.translation: Es más, la misma vista puede utilizarse en la llamada semanal.

questions.question: Two observations deserve the same level of attention. Which connector communicates that?
options: In an equal important way, decisions need a consistent form to be registered by the team.
Same importantly, the team needs one consistent way of record the decisions.
Equally important, the team needs a consistent way to record decisions.
With equal importance, the team needs a consistent manner for registering decisions.
questions.explanation: «Equally important,» indica que la nueva idea tiene el mismo peso que la anterior. «A consistent way to record» es claro y natural.
questions.translation: Igualmente importante, el equipo necesita una forma coherente de registrar las decisiones.

questions.question: A presenter wants to add evidence without interrupting the flow. Which version is best?
options: We saw also the same pattern on the reporting period previous.
We also saw the same pattern in the previous reporting period.
Also we have seen that equal pattern in the anterior period of reporting.
We as well did see the same pattern during the period before of reports.
questions.explanation: Con un verbo léxico, «also» suele ir antes del verbo principal: «also saw». «Previous reporting period» mantiene un orden nominal natural.
questions.translation: También observamos el mismo patrón en el periodo de informes anterior.

questions.question: You need to append a final supporting point to a recommendation. Choose the clearest sentence.
options: On the top of that, the change does not require additional formation to the customer team.
At the top of this, the customer team requires no training in addition for the change.
On top of that, the change requires no additional training for the customer team.
Over that, no additional training is required by the change for the team of customer.
questions.explanation: «On top of that» es un conector hablado natural para añadir apoyo. La expresión es sin «the», y «training» suele ser incontable.
questions.translation: Además, el cambio no requiere formación adicional para el equipo del cliente.

questions.question: Which option adds a formal supporting point appropriately in a steering-committee presentation?
options: Further, the proposed schedule is giving to both teams time enough to prepare.
Furthermore to this, the proposed schedule gives enough time to both teams for preparing themselves.
For furthermore, both teams have sufficient time of preparation with the schedule proposed.
Furthermore, the proposed schedule gives both teams enough time to prepare.
questions.explanation: «Furthermore,» puede introducir una idea adicional en un registro formal. «Gives both teams enough time to prepare» coloca los elementos de forma natural.
questions.translation: Además, el calendario propuesto da a ambos equipos tiempo suficiente para prepararse.

questions.question: The number of alerts fell, but the investigation workload did not. Which sentence expresses the contrast clearly?
options: Alert volumes decreased, but however the investigation workload was remaining similar.
Alert volumes decreased; however, the investigation workload remained broadly unchanged.
Alert volumes decreased; although, the investigation workload remained broadly unchanged.
Alert volumes decreased; nevertheless of this, the investigation workload stayed widely unchanged.
questions.explanation: «However» puede conectar dos ideas completas y va bien tras punto y coma. «Although» necesita introducir una oración subordinada, no funciona solo como adverbio.
questions.translation: El volumen de alertas disminuyó; sin embargo, la carga de trabajo de investigación se mantuvo prácticamente sin cambios.

questions.question: You agree that the dashboard is useful, then want to mention a limitation. Choose the most natural transition.
options: The dashboard is useful. With that being said it, each case's history is not full shown.
The dashboard is useful. Said that, it does not show the complete historic of each case.
The dashboard is useful. Having that said, it is not showing all the history for every case.
The dashboard is useful. That said, it does not show the full history of each case.
questions.explanation: «That said,» introduce una reserva después de reconocer un punto positivo. Es una fórmula natural y más concisa que las traducciones literales.
questions.translation: El panel es útil. Dicho esto, no muestra el historial completo de cada caso.

questions.question: Complete the balanced sentence: '___ the overall trend is positive, two areas still need attention.'
options: However
In spite
Despite
While
questions.explanation: «While» puede introducir una oración con sujeto y verbo para contrastarla con la principal. «Despite» e «in spite of» requieren un sintagma nominal o gerundio.
questions.translation: Aunque la tendencia general es positiva, todavía hay dos áreas que requieren atención.

questions.question: Which version acknowledges a constraint without weakening the conclusion unnecessarily?
options: Even the sample being limited, yet it gives an useful indication on the trend.
Although the sample is limited, it still provides a useful indication of the trend.
Although of the limited sample, it still provides a useful indication about the tendency.
Despite the sample is limited, it provides still one useful indication of the trend.
questions.explanation: «Although» va seguido de una oración completa. «A useful indication of the trend» y la posición de «still» resultan naturales.
questions.translation: Aunque la muestra es limitada, sigue ofreciendo una indicación útil de la tendencia.

questions.question: You are comparing two reporting approaches, with no implication that one is always better. Choose the neutral contrast.
options: The weekly report gives more detail. On the other hand, the dashboard is easier to explore interactively.
The weekly report gives more detail. In the other hand, the dashboard is easier for exploring interactively.
The weekly report gives more detail. On another hand, the dashboard is more easy to explore interactively.
The weekly report gives more detail. By the other side, the dashboard explores more easily in an interactive way.
questions.explanation: La expresión fija es «on the other hand». Presenta una perspectiva alternativa sin convertirla necesariamente en una contradicción.
questions.translation: El informe semanal ofrece más detalle. Por otro lado, el panel es más fácil de explorar de forma interactiva.

questions.question: Two customer groups behaved differently. Which sentence highlights the contrast most directly?
options: The first group requested detail. On contrast, a summary shorter was preferred from the second.
The first group requested more detail. In contrast to, the second preferred a more short summary.
The first group asked more detail. By contrary, the second was preferring a shorter resume.
The first group requested more detail. By contrast, the second preferred a shorter summary.
questions.explanation: «By contrast,» compara resultados claramente diferentes. «Prefer» se construye directamente con el objeto: «preferred a shorter summary».
questions.translation: El primer grupo solicitó más detalle. En cambio, el segundo prefirió un resumen más breve.

questions.question: Complete the sentence correctly: '___ the short notice, both teams were able to attend.'
options: Even though of
However
Despite
Although
questions.explanation: «Despite» va seguido de un sintagma nominal: «the short notice». «Although» y «even though» necesitarían una oración con verbo.
questions.translation: A pesar del poco tiempo de aviso, ambos equipos pudieron asistir.

questions.question: The customer expected a delay, but the report arrived on time. Which wording is most natural?
options: The timeline was tight; nevertheless of that, the report delivered itself according to schedule.
The timeline was tight; nevertheless, the report was delivered on schedule.
The timeline was tight, despite the report was delivered on schedule.
The timeline was tight; even though, the report was delivered in the scheduled time.
questions.explanation: «Nevertheless» funciona como adverbio de contraste y no lleva «of that». «Delivered on schedule» es la colocación natural.
questions.translation: El plazo era ajustado; aun así, el informe se entregó según lo previsto.

questions.question: You want to replace an inaccurate claim with a more precise one. Choose the best contrast structure.
options: Rather than showing a confirmed outcome, the chart highlights activity that needs further review.
Rather that it shows an outcome confirmed, the chart highlights activity which needs being reviewed more.
More than showing a confirmed result, the chart is highlighting activity to review furtherly.
Instead to show a confirmed outcome, the chart highlights activity needing of further review.
questions.explanation: «Rather than + -ing» contrasta la interpretación descartada con la correcta. «Needs further review» es conciso y natural.
questions.translation: En lugar de mostrar un resultado confirmado, el gráfico destaca actividad que necesita una revisión adicional.

questions.question: Which sentence concedes a point and then keeps the discussion moving?
options: Despite the change is small, it deserves explaining it because the customers will realize it.
Even the change is small, it is worthy to explain because customers will notice it.
Even though the change is small, it is worth explaining because customers will notice it.
Although of being a small change, it is worth to explain as customers are noticing it.
questions.explanation: «Even though» introduce una oración completa. La expresión correcta es «it is worth explaining», sin infinitivo ni objeto repetido.
questions.translation: Aunque el cambio es pequeño, merece la pena explicarlo porque los clientes lo notarán.

questions.question: Complete the customer update: 'The meeting started late ___ an earlier call overran.'
options: because of
because
due to
as a result of
questions.explanation: «Because» introduce una oración completa: «an earlier call overran». Las otras opciones necesitan un sustantivo o sintagma nominal.
questions.translation: La reunión empezó tarde porque una llamada anterior se alargó.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct explanation of a reporting delay.
options: The report was delayed because of a problem with the source data.
The report was delayed because a problem with the source data.
The report was delayed due to the source data had a problem.
The report delayed as result of there was a problem with source data.
questions.explanation: «Because of» va seguido de un sintagma nominal: «a problem with the source data». Para una oración completa se usaría «because».
questions.translation: El informe se retrasó debido a un problema con los datos de origen.

questions.question: A revised process removed one manual step. What is the clearest way to state the result?
options: As a consequence of, the team is able to prepare quicker the customer update.
As a result, the team can prepare the customer update more quickly.
For this result, the customer update can be prepared by the team in a quicker manner.
As result, the team can prepare more quickly the update of customer.
questions.explanation: «As a result,» presenta una consecuencia y funciona como conector independiente. «Prepare the update more quickly» mantiene un orden natural.
questions.translation: Como resultado, el equipo puede preparar la actualización para el cliente más rápidamente.

questions.question: The evidence is incomplete. Choose the most professional conclusion.
options: Due to the evidence is incomplete, therefore we must present preliminarily the finding.
The available evidence is incomplete; therefore, we should present the finding as preliminary.
The available evidences are incomplete; therefore we should present the finding like preliminary.
The evidence available is incomplete, so therefore the finding should be presented as a preliminar one.
questions.explanation: «Therefore» enlaza causa y conclusión con precisión. «Evidence» es incontable y la expresión natural es «present the finding as preliminary».
questions.translation: Las evidencias disponibles son incompletas; por tanto, deberíamos presentar el hallazgo como preliminar.

questions.question: Which spoken explanation makes the consequence clear to a non-technical audience?
options: The timestamps are in different hours, meaning us that we must align before comparing the events.
The time zones differ, which wants to say we need to make them aligned previous to compare events.
The timestamps use different time zones, which means that we need to align them before comparing events.
The timestamps use different time zones, what means that we need aligning them before to compare events.
questions.explanation: «Which means that...» explica la consecuencia de toda la idea anterior. Después de «before» es natural usar gerundio: «before comparing».
questions.translation: Las marcas de tiempo utilizan zonas horarias diferentes, lo que significa que debemos alinearlas antes de comparar los eventos.

questions.question: Complete the slide commentary: 'Response times improved ___ the simpler approval route.'
options: therefore
due to
because
which means
questions.explanation: «Due to» va seguido de un sintagma nominal: «the simpler approval route». «Because» necesitaría una oración completa.
questions.translation: Los tiempos de respuesta mejoraron gracias al proceso de aprobación más sencillo.

questions.question: You need a natural, conversational link between a missing input and a delayed decision. Which option fits?
options: We haven't received yet the final figures, so that we'll confirm tomorrow the decision.
The final figures are not received already, that's because we confirm the decision on tomorrow.
We haven't received the final figures yet, so we'll confirm the decision tomorrow.
We didn't receive the final figures still, therefore so the decision confirms tomorrow.
questions.explanation: «So» introduce una consecuencia de forma natural en conversación. «Yet» suele ir al final y «tomorrow» no lleva «on».
questions.translation: Todavía no hemos recibido las cifras definitivas, así que confirmaremos la decisión mañana.

questions.question: Which sentence describes a possible effect without overstating certainty?
options: A gap in the data could lead to an incomplete view of the timeline.
A gap of data may result an incomplete timeline view for sure.
A data gap could derive to the timeline having one vision incomplete.
A gap in the data could lead into an incomplete view about the timeline.
questions.explanation: La colocación es «lead to + noun». «Could» expresa posibilidad y evita presentar el efecto como seguro.
questions.translation: Una laguna en los datos podría dar lugar a una visión incompleta de la cronología.

questions.question: You have explained that one chart combines several sources. How do you state the practical consequence?
options: Consequently, small differences in timing may appear in the combined view.
Consequently of this, small differences of timing may appear on the view combined.
In consequence to this, the combined view might shows small differences in timings.
As consequence, little timing differences can be appeared in the combined vision.
questions.explanation: «Consequently,» introduce el efecto en un registro formal. «May appear» no necesita pasiva y «combined view» mantiene el orden correcto.
questions.translation: En consecuencia, pueden aparecer pequeñas diferencias temporales en la vista combinada.

questions.question: A customer asks why you are changing the order of the presentation. Choose the clearest reply.
options: The team is leaving early; this is the motive why their actions are covered the first.
Because the team has to leave early, for that we are covering their actions in first place.
The operations team has to leave early, which is why we're covering their actions first.
The operations team must leave before, so that's because we cover first their actions.
questions.explanation: «Which is why...» conecta la causa con la decisión sin redundancia. «Covering their actions first» coloca el adverbio correctamente.
questions.translation: El equipo de operaciones tiene que marcharse antes, así que por eso vamos a tratar primero sus acciones.

questions.question: You want to illustrate what counts as a communication issue. Choose the best example marker.
options: For an example, an unclear owner can delay the next update even the action itself is simple.
For example, an unclear owner can delay the next update even when the action itself is simple.
As example, a not clear owner may delay the following update despite of the simple action.
By example, the next update can be delayed from an unclear owner, also when the action is simple.
questions.explanation: «For example,» es la fórmula estándar para introducir una ilustración. «Even when» introduce correctamente la circunstancia contrastante.
questions.translation: Por ejemplo, no tener un responsable claro puede retrasar la siguiente actualización incluso cuando la acción en sí es sencilla.

questions.question: A customer looks confused by the phrase 'single source of truth'. How would you restate it?
options: With other words, everybody should use the same accorded information when discussing about the case.
In other words, everyone should use the same agreed information when discussing the case.
Said in another words, all people must use an equal information for discussing the case.
In other word, everyone should use one same agreed information when they discuss on the case.
questions.explanation: «In other words,» introduce una reformulación. «Discuss the case» no lleva «about», y «information» es incontable.
questions.translation: En otras palabras, todos deberían utilizar la misma información acordada al hablar del caso.

questions.question: Choose the clearest plain-English explanation for an executive audience.
options: To put it in a simple way, the chart is showing where the team spent the most part of its time.
Putting it simple, the chart displays where did the team spend the majority of their time.
To put it simply, the chart shows where the team spent most of its time.
For saying it simply, the graphic shows in where the team expended most time.
questions.explanation: «To put it simply» señala una explicación sencilla. La interrogativa indirecta usa «where the team spent», no el orden de pregunta.
questions.translation: Dicho de forma sencilla, el gráfico muestra dónde dedicó el equipo la mayor parte de su tiempo.

questions.question: A client asks what you mean by 'open action'. Which reply is most natural?
options: What I want to mean by open action is one task which has agreed and has not yet complete.
By open action, what I mean is a task that was accorded but it is pending to complete.
What I mean by an open action is a task that has been agreed but not yet completed.
What I mean with an open action is a task agreed but not completed still.
questions.explanation: La estructura natural es «what I mean by X is...». «Not yet completed» expresa con claridad que la tarea sigue pendiente.
questions.translation: Con acción abierta me refiero a una tarea que se ha acordado pero todavía no se ha completado.

questions.question: You need to narrow a general statement to one precise concern. Which signpost works best?
options: In a more specification, the concern concerns about the recording of ownership in ticket.
More specific, the concern is related with how is ownership recorded in the ticket.
Speaking more specifically, the worry has relation to how the ownership records itself on the ticket.
More specifically, the concern relates to how ownership is recorded in the ticket.
questions.explanation: «More specifically,» permite pasar de lo general a lo concreto. La colocación es «relates to» y la interrogativa indirecta mantiene «how ownership is recorded».
questions.translation: Más concretamente, la preocupación se refiere a cómo se registra la responsabilidad en el ticket.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'The pack includes operational measures, ___ response time and case age.'
options: for example of
like for example
such like
such as
questions.explanation: «Such as» introduce ejemplos dentro de un sintagma nominal. No necesita «for example» ni se combina con «like».
questions.translation: El paquete incluye medidas operativas, como el tiempo de respuesta y la antigüedad de los casos.

questions.question: A slide contains an abstract recommendation. What is the best spoken bridge to a concrete scenario?
options: Let me give to you one practical example about how would that look like.
Let me put you an example in practice of what would it look like.
Let me give you a practical example of what that would look like.
Allow me giving you a practical example of how that would be looking.
questions.explanation: «Let me give you a practical example...» es una fórmula natural. En una interrogativa indirecta se dice «what that would look like».
questions.translation: Permítanme darles un ejemplo práctico de cómo sería eso.

questions.question: The customer may interpret 'closed' as 'fully resolved'. Which clarification is clearest?
options: To be clear, 'closed' here means that the SOC review is complete, not that every related action is finished.
For being clear, 'closed' here wants to say the SOC review is complete, not every action related is finished.
Being clear, by 'closed' we are meaning the review completed instead of every related action finished.
To clarify us, 'closed' signifies here that review is complete, not that all related action has finished.
questions.explanation: «To be clear» evita una interpretación errónea de forma directa. La estructura paralela «that..., not that...» distingue los dos significados.
questions.translation: Para que quede claro, aquí «cerrado» significa que la revisión del SOC ha terminado, no que todas las acciones relacionadas hayan finalizado.

questions.question: Choose the phrase that translates a policy statement into its practical effect.
options: In terms of practice, it means that one consolidated update will arrive to the customer.
In practical terms, this wants to say that the customer will receive one update consolidated.
In practical terms, this means that the customer will receive one consolidated update.
On practice, this means the customer is going to receive an unique consolidated update.
questions.explanation: «In practical terms» introduce la consecuencia concreta. «One consolidated update» mantiene el orden natural de los adjetivos.
questions.translation: En términos prácticos, esto significa que el cliente recibirá una única actualización consolidada.

questions.question: You need to identify exactly which two actions require approval. Which wording is most precise?
options: Concretely, we need the approval for changing the schedule and publish the template revised.
In specific, we require that approval is given for the schedule change and to publishing the template.
Specifically speaking, it is needed approval to change schedule and for publishing the revised template.
Specifically, we need approval to change the schedule and to publish the revised template.
questions.explanation: «Specifically,» enfoca la lista concreta. Los dos infinitivos «to change» y «to publish» forman una estructura paralela clara.
questions.translation: En concreto, necesitamos aprobación para cambiar el calendario y publicar la plantilla revisada.

questions.question: You need to remind the audience of a definition given earlier. Which phrase sounds natural?
options: As I mentioned earlier, we use 'case age' to mean the time since the case was opened.
Like I told earlier, 'case age' is used to mean the time from the case has opened.
As I mentioned before ago, we use 'case age' for meaning the time since the case opened.
As mentioned by me previously, we are using 'case age' to say the time since opening the case.
questions.explanation: «As I mentioned earlier» remite atrás de forma natural y discreta. «The time since the case was opened» expresa correctamente el periodo.
questions.translation: Como mencioné antes, utilizamos «antigüedad del caso» para referirnos al tiempo transcurrido desde que se abrió.

questions.question: A detailed question belongs in a later section. How can you postpone it politely?
options: I'll come back to that when we look at the investigation timeline.
I will retake that point when we look into the timeline later on after.
I will return back to that when we will look the timeline of investigation.
I come back with that once we are seeing the investigation's timeline.
questions.explanation: «I'll come back to that...» aplaza la respuesta sin ignorarla. Tras «when» para el futuro se usa presente: «when we look», no «will look».
questions.translation: Volveré a ese punto cuando veamos la cronología de la investigación.

questions.question: You want the audience to focus on a visual. Choose the standard presentation phrase.
options: As you can see in this slide, the most of actions completed inside the agreed timeframe.
As you can see on this slide, most actions were completed within the agreed timeframe.
Like it can be seen on this slide, most of the actions were completed into the time agreed.
As you are seeing at the slide, the majority actions got completed within timeframe accorded.
questions.explanation: «As you can see on this slide» dirige la atención a la pantalla. «Most actions» no lleva «the» y «within the agreed timeframe» es natural.
questions.translation: Como pueden ver en esta diapositiva, la mayoría de las acciones se completaron dentro del plazo acordado.

questions.question: You have introduced a risk and now reach the slide where it becomes relevant. What would you say?
options: It is in this part that the earlier data quality point gets importance.
This is when the previous point over data quality becomes of importance.
This is where the earlier point about data quality becomes important.
Here is where the point before about data quality turns itself important.
questions.explanation: «This is where...» conecta una idea previa con el punto actual. «The earlier point about...» es claro y no suena traducido literalmente.
questions.translation: Aquí es donde cobra importancia el punto anterior sobre la calidad de los datos.

questions.question: Before leaving a section, you want to revisit one unresolved detail. Choose the smoothest wording.
options: Before we continue ahead, let me retake in brief the question of who owns.
Previous to pass on, I want to come again shortly over the ownership question.
Before we move on, let me return briefly to the question of ownership.
Before moving forward, let me return back briefly at the question about ownership.
questions.explanation: «Before we move on» pausa la progresión y «return to the question of...» recupera el tema sin redundancia. «Return back» duplica la idea.
questions.translation: Antes de continuar, permítanme volver brevemente a la cuestión de la responsabilidad.

questions.question: You mention a term now but plan to define it on the next slide. What is the clearest signpost?
options: In one moment, I am going to explain about what means 'coverage gap' for us.
I'll explain what we mean by 'coverage gap' in a moment.
I will explain shortly what are we meaning by 'coverage gap'.
I explain in a moment what do we mean with 'coverage gap'.
questions.explanation: «In a moment» señala que la explicación llegará enseguida. La interrogativa indirecta usa «what we mean», sin inversión.
questions.translation: En un momento explicaré qué entendemos por «laguna de cobertura».

questions.question: The previous speaker described the business impact. You want to connect your section to it. Which opening works best?
options: Building on that point, I'd like to show how the reporting change supports the customer team.
Constructing from that point, I like to show how the change of reporting supports to the customer team.
Based in that point, let me show how is the customer team supported by the reporting change.
Building over that point, I would like showing how does the reporting change support the team.
questions.explanation: «Building on that point» enlaza con la intervención anterior. En la subordinada se mantiene «how the change supports», sin inversión.
questions.translation: Partiendo de ese punto, me gustaría mostrar cómo el cambio en los informes ayuda al equipo del cliente.

questions.question: You want to remind the audience of a chart shown ten minutes ago. Choose the most natural reference.
options: If you remember it, the chart of before showed a gradual decline instead than a sudden drop.
If you recall, the earlier chart showed a gradual decline rather than a sudden drop.
If you recall yourself, that former chart showed gradually declining rather than dropping suddenly.
As you may recall it, the previous graphic was showing a decline gradual and not one sudden fall.
questions.explanation: «If you recall» recuerda información compartida sin exigir objeto. «Rather than» contrasta dos sintagmas paralelos.
questions.translation: Si recuerdan, el gráfico anterior mostraba un descenso gradual, no una caída repentina.

questions.question: A later slide will show the evidence behind your conclusion. Which phrase prepares the audience?
options: As we'll see shortly, the conclusion is supported by three separate observations.
As we will see soon later, the conclusion is supported from three observations separated.
Like we'll be seeing shortly, three separated observations are supporting to the conclusion.
As it will be seen after a short time, the conclusion has support by three separate observations.
questions.explanation: «As we'll see shortly» anticipa contenido próximo. «Supported by» y «three separate observations» son combinaciones naturales.
questions.translation: Como veremos enseguida, la conclusión está respaldada por tres observaciones distintas.

questions.question: You are connecting the closing recommendation to an issue raised at the start. Which sentence is clearest?
options: That is linking again to the concern we put at the start from the session.
That links back to the concern we raised at the beginning of the session.
That links back with the concern that we rose in the beginning of the session.
This makes a link backwards to the worry raised on the session's beginning.
questions.explanation: «Link back to» remite de forma explícita a una idea anterior. El pasado de «raise» es «raised», y se dice «at the beginning».
questions.translation: Eso enlaza con la preocupación que planteamos al principio de la sesión.

questions.question: You need to ensure the customer remembers one central message. Which signpost is strongest and most natural?
options: The key point is about the trend being stable, even individual weeks are varying.
The point key is that the tendency remains stable, although of variations in individual weeks.
The principal key point says the trend is stable in spite individual weeks vary.
The key point is that the trend is stable, even though individual weeks vary.
questions.explanation: «The key point is that...» presenta el mensaje central directamente. «Even though» introduce una oración completa de contraste.
questions.translation: El punto clave es que la tendencia es estable, aunque las semanas individuales varíen.

questions.question: Three improvements are listed, but one has the greatest customer impact. Choose the best emphasis marker.
options: In the most important way, one single contact point is provided for the customer by the process.
More important, the process revised is giving the customer a point of contact single.
The most importantly, the revised process gives to the customer one unique contact point.
Most importantly, the revised process gives the customer a single point of contact.
questions.explanation: «Most importantly,» destaca la idea prioritaria. Con «give» el receptor va antes del objeto: «gives the customer a...».
questions.translation: Y lo más importante: el proceso revisado ofrece al cliente un único punto de contacto.

questions.question: An executive asks which detail matters for the decision. What is the clearest reply?
options: What matters here is whether the proposed date works for both teams.
What matters here is if does the proposed date work for both teams.
The thing which imports here is whether works the proposed date for the two teams.
What is mattering in here is whether the date proposed is working to both teams.
questions.explanation: «What matters here is whether...» enfoca el criterio decisivo. La interrogativa indirecta conserva «the proposed date works».
questions.translation: Lo que importa aquí es si la fecha propuesta funciona para ambos equipos.

questions.question: You want to direct attention to one number on a busy slide. Which phrase is appropriate?
options: I'd like to draw your attention to the figure in the top-right corner.
I want to attract the attention of you to the number in the superior-right corner.
I would like to call your attention on the figure at the corner up right.
Let me put your attention over the figure located on the top right corner.
questions.explanation: La expresión estándar es «draw your attention to». Para la posición se dice «in the top-right corner».
questions.translation: Me gustaría llamar su atención sobre la cifra de la esquina superior derecha.

questions.question: Complete the sentence naturally: 'The new summary is ___ useful for readers who only need the main decisions.'
options: in special
more particularly of
especially
specially
questions.explanation: «Especially» destaca a un grupo concreto. «Specially» suele significar «de manera especial» o «para un propósito específico» y no encaja igual aquí.
questions.translation: El nuevo resumen es útil especialmente para quienes solo necesitan las decisiones principales.

questions.question: You want to stress a principle that should guide all the next steps. Choose the best formulation.
options: Over all, the next steps need being clear for the people responsible to carry them.
Above everything, next steps have the need to be clear to people in charge of making them out.
On top all, the following steps must clearly arrive to those responsible of executing them.
Above all, the next steps need to be clear to the people responsible for carrying them out.
questions.explanation: «Above all,» da máxima prioridad a la idea. «Responsible for» va seguido de gerundio: «for carrying them out».
questions.translation: Por encima de todo, los próximos pasos deben estar claros para las personas responsables de llevarlos a cabo.

questions.question: Choose the most natural way to state the main conclusion at the end of a section.
options: The main take away of this section is that a clearer ownership leads into a faster follow-up.
The principal conclusion to take from this section says clearer ownership makes follow-up more fast.
The main takeaway from this section is that clearer ownership leads to faster follow-up.
The main learning from the section is about clear ownership conducting to quicker following.
questions.explanation: «The main takeaway from...» resume la conclusión que debe retenerse. «Leads to» es la preposición correcta.
questions.translation: La principal conclusión de esta sección es que una responsabilidad más clara permite un seguimiento más rápido.

questions.question: A customer asks what must be resolved during today's call. Which answer prioritises clearly?
options: Our priority for today is to agree on the owner and the target date.
Our priority of today is agreeing the responsible and the objective date.
Today we have as priority that the owner and the date target are accorded.
The priority for today consists in to agree about the owner and target date.
questions.explanation: «Our priority for today is to...» presenta un objetivo concreto. Se dice «agree on» y «target date».
questions.translation: Nuestra prioridad para hoy es acordar el responsable y la fecha objetivo.

questions.question: You need to highlight a caveat without making it sound alarming. What would you say?
options: It is worthy to note that the figures are covering only labour days.
It deserves to be noted the figures cover business days solely only.
It's worth noting that the figures cover business days only.
It has value to notice that figures just cover the days that are business.
questions.explanation: «It's worth noting that...» llama la atención sobre un matiz de forma neutral. La construcción exige gerundio: «worth noting».
questions.translation: Conviene señalar que las cifras solo abarcan días laborables.

questions.question: The audience may remember the chart but miss its limitation. Choose the professional emphasis.
options: I want to make emphasis that this chart shows a direction, not one precise forecast.
I would insist in that this graphic shows the direction and not exactly a prediction.
I want to stress that this chart shows direction, not a precise forecast.
I want stressing that the chart is showing direction instead a forecast precise.
questions.explanation: «I want to stress that...» es una forma directa y profesional de enfatizar. «Make emphasis» es un calco; en inglés se usa «emphasise» o «stress».
questions.translation: Quiero subrayar que este gráfico muestra una dirección, no una previsión precisa.

questions.question: A customer asks a detailed question during your presentation. Which opening acknowledges it professionally?
options: This is a good question. Let me separate what do we know from what needs still confirmation.
That's a good question. Let me separate what we know from what still needs to be confirmed.
That is one good question. I will divide the known things and what stays for confirming.
Good question. Let me distinguish what we are knowing from what remains to confirm yet.
questions.explanation: «That's a good question» reconoce la intervención. Las interrogativas indirectas usan «what we know», sin inversión.
questions.translation: Es una buena pregunta. Permítanme separar lo que sabemos de lo que todavía debe confirmarse.

questions.question: You want to check that you understood the customer's concern. Choose the most natural response.
options: If I understood you correctly, you are asking if does the change affect the weekly report.
If I understand you correctly, you're asking whether the change affects the weekly report.
If I understand correctly to you, you ask if the change has affectation on the report weekly.
If I am understanding well, your question is whether affects the change to the weekly report.
questions.explanation: «If I understand you correctly...» verifica la interpretación con cortesía. La interrogativa indirecta conserva «the change affects».
questions.translation: Si le he entendido bien, pregunta si el cambio afecta al informe semanal.

questions.question: You do not know an exact percentage during a meeting. Which answer is most credible?
options: I don't have that figure to hand, but I'll check it and include it in the follow-up.
I don't have that figure in the hand, but I will look it and include on the follow-up.
I haven't this exact percentage with me, but I'll revise and put it in the posterior mail.
The figure is not available for me now; however I suppose it can be added afterwards.
questions.explanation: «I don't have that figure to hand» reconoce la limitación sin improvisar. «Check it» y «include it in the follow-up» ofrecen una acción concreta.
questions.translation: No tengo esa cifra a mano, pero la comprobaré y la incluiré en el seguimiento.

questions.question: The analysis is still in progress. Which statement uses an appropriately cautious tone?
options: According with current information, the activity is definitely limited to only one account.
From the informations we have, it looks that the activity limits itself at one account.
Based on the information available so far, the activity appears to be limited to one account.
Basing on the information available until now, the activity seems being limited in one account.
questions.explanation: «Based on the information available so far» delimita la evidencia, y «appears to be» expresa una conclusión provisional sin exagerar certeza.
questions.translation: Según la información disponible hasta ahora, la actividad parece limitarse a una sola cuenta.

questions.question: You need to state the current understanding while leaving room for new evidence. Choose the best phrase.
options: To our better knowledge, any other systems are affected at the actual stage.
For the best of our knowledge, no other systems result affected in this stage.
To the best of our knowledge, no other systems are affected at this stage.
As far as our best knowing, there are not affected other systems for the moment.
questions.explanation: «To the best of our knowledge» comunica cautela profesional. «At this stage» deja claro que la evaluación puede cambiar.
questions.translation: Hasta donde sabemos, no hay otros sistemas afectados en esta fase.

questions.question: A question is ambiguous. How should you ask for precision?
options: Could you clarify what you mean by 'full coverage' in this context?
Could you explain me what are you meaning by the full coverage in this case?
Can you make clear what means for you 'full coverage' on this context?
Could you clarify what do you mean with 'full coverage' in this context?
questions.explanation: «Could you clarify what you mean by...?» es cortés y específico. En la interrogativa indirecta no se usa «do».
questions.translation: ¿Podría aclarar qué quiere decir con «cobertura completa» en este contexto?

questions.question: The customer asks whether a date is final, but another team owns the confirmation. What is the best reply?
options: The date continues being provisional. I'll contrast it to the project team and answer later.
The date is yet provisional. I will verify with the project team and revert after the call.
It is a provisional date still; I will confirm them with the project team and return you after the call.
The date is still provisional. I'll verify it with the project team and follow up after the call.
questions.explanation: La respuesta distingue el estado actual de la acción posterior. «Verify it with...» y «follow up after the call» son claros y naturales internacionalmente.
questions.translation: La fecha sigue siendo provisional. La verificaré con el equipo de proyecto y haré seguimiento después de la llamada.

questions.question: You want to confirm a multi-part request before answering. Which sentence sounds most natural?
options: Let me verify my understanding: you are needing the trend, change reason, and action proposition, yes?
Allow me to check that I have understood you well: the trend, why did it change, and proposed action. Correct?
Let me check if I understood: you need the trend, the motive of change, and the action proposed. Isn't it?
Let me check that I've understood: you need the trend, the reason for the change, and the proposed action. Is that right?
questions.explanation: «Let me check that I've understood...» resume antes de responder y «Is that right?» solicita confirmación de forma natural.
questions.translation: Permítame comprobar que lo he entendido: necesita la tendencia, el motivo del cambio y la acción propuesta. ¿Es correcto?

questions.question: Some facts are confirmed, but the root cause is not. Which wording separates certainty levels clearly?
options: We can say confidently the service interrupted; the cause underneath continues under investigation.
We can say with confidence that the service was interrupted; the underlying cause is still being investigated.
We are confident to say that service was interrupted, but the root cause is investigating still.
With confidence we can tell the interruption, while the underlying reason remains to be investigated yet.
questions.explanation: «We can say with confidence that...» presenta el hecho confirmado. El punto y coma separa con claridad la parte todavía abierta.
questions.translation: Podemos afirmar con seguridad que el servicio se interrumpió; la causa subyacente sigue investigándose.

questions.question: A participant asks you to guess why another team made a decision. Choose the most professional response.
options: I wouldn't want to speculate. Let me confirm the rationale with the team and come back to you.
I don't want making speculations. I will ask the rationale with the team and revert you.
I wouldn't like to speculate it. Let me confirm the motive to the team and return back to you.
I prefer not to invent. Let me contrast why with the team and come back with you.
questions.explanation: «I wouldn't want to speculate» evita una suposición sin sonar defensivo. «Confirm ... with the team» y «come back to you» ofrecen un seguimiento claro.
questions.translation: No quisiera especular. Permítame confirmar el razonamiento con el equipo y volver a contactar con usted.

questions.question: You are ending a detailed presentation. Which phrase introduces a concise summary?
options: Summing everything, performance remained stably, two actions have completion, and one decision waits.
To sum up, performance remained stable, two actions were completed, and one decision is still pending.
To make a summary, the performance was stable, there were two completed actions and a decision pending still.
For summing up, performance kept stable, two actions completed, and one decision remains yet pending.
questions.explanation: «To sum up,» señala el resumen final. La enumeración mantiene tres estructuras breves y claras.
questions.translation: En resumen, el rendimiento se mantuvo estable, se completaron dos acciones y todavía hay una decisión pendiente.

questions.question: After a long explanation, you want to give the one-sentence version. Choose the best signpost.
options: In shorts, the process works, but the handover needs being more clear.
On a short way, the process works well, but it needs to clarify more the handover.
Saying it shortly, the process is functioning, however the handover needs more clarity to be.
In short, the process is working, but the handover needs to be clearer.
questions.explanation: «In short,» introduce una síntesis muy breve. «Needs to be clearer» es una estructura natural y paralela.
questions.translation: En pocas palabras, el proceso funciona, pero el traspaso debe ser más claro.

questions.question: You want to check for unresolved matters before ending the meeting. What would you say?
options: Before we close, is there anything we haven't covered that needs a decision today?
Before that we finish, is anything missing to cover requiring a decision for today?
Before closing, is there something we didn't cover and needs a decision in today?
Previous to close, have we any point not covered which needs to be decided today?
questions.explanation: «Before we close...» anticipa el final y abre un último espacio de decisión. «Anything we haven't covered» resulta natural en una pregunta.
questions.translation: Antes de terminar, ¿hay algo que no hayamos tratado y que necesite una decisión hoy?

questions.question: Choose the clearest recap of three decisions made during the call.
options: To recap, we've agreed on the owner, the target date, and the format of the next update.
To make a recap, we have accorded about the owner, the date target, and the following update format.
For recapping, we agreed the owner, objective date, and how will be the next update's format.
Recapitulating, agreement was made on who owns, when targets, and what format has the update.
questions.explanation: «To recap» es una señal habitual al final de una reunión. La lista usa tres sintagmas nominales paralelos y «agree on».
questions.translation: Recapitulando, hemos acordado el responsable, la fecha objetivo y el formato de la próxima actualización.

questions.question: What is the most natural way to state the central message one last time?
options: The main takeout is clearer signposting will do the customer update easier to follow.
The principal takeaway is about signposting more clearly for making easier the update to follow.
The main message to take is that clearer signals make more easy following the customer update.
The main takeaway is that clearer signposting will make the customer update easier to follow.
questions.explanation: «The main takeaway is that...» vuelve a fijar la idea principal. «Make the update easier to follow» usa correctamente «make + objeto + adjetivo».
questions.translation: La conclusión principal es que una señalización más clara hará que la actualización para el cliente sea más fácil de seguir.

questions.question: You are assigning follow-up work. Which closing statement is most precise?
options: The next steps consist to update the timeline, confirm to the owner, and sending the pack before Friday.
As next steps, we have to update timeline, confirming ownership, and send the revised pack for Friday.
The next steps are to update the timeline, confirm the owner, and send the revised pack by Friday.
The following steps are updating the timeline, to confirm the owner, and sending the pack revised until Friday.
questions.explanation: Tras «are to» aparecen tres infinitivos paralelos: «update, confirm, send». «By Friday» fija una fecha límite inclusiva.
questions.translation: Los próximos pasos son actualizar la cronología, confirmar el responsable y enviar el paquete revisado a más tardar el viernes.

questions.question: You have reached the final slide. Which sentence closes the content cleanly before questions?
options: That covers all points I wanted discussing today. I am happy for taking questions.
With that are covered the points I wanted to speak today. You can make questions now.
That covers the points I wanted to discuss today. I'm happy to take any questions.
Those were the points to discuss for today. I will be pleased that you ask any doubts.
questions.explanation: «That covers...» indica que el contenido ha terminado y «I'm happy to take any questions» abre el turno de preguntas de manera profesional.
questions.translation: Con esto quedan cubiertos los puntos que quería tratar hoy. Estaré encantada de responder a sus preguntas.

questions.question: No one has additional questions. Choose the most natural way to move to the close.
options: If there are no further questions, let's confirm the actions before we finish.
If no further questions exist, we confirm the actions previous to finishing.
If there aren't more questions, let's confirm the actions before to finish.
In case there are not additional doubts, let's make confirmation of the actions before finish.
questions.explanation: «If there are no further questions...» es una transición cortés al cierre. Después de «before» se usa una oración o gerundio, no «to finish».
questions.translation: Si no hay más preguntas, confirmemos las acciones antes de terminar.

questions.question: Which final thank-you sounds warm but professional?
options: Thank you for your time and for the helpful input today.
Thank you for your time and for the useful inputs of today.
I appreciate your time and the helps you have provided during today.
Thanks for spending your time and giving helpful opinions in today's date.
questions.explanation: «Thank you for your time and for the helpful input» es natural; «input» suele ser incontable en este sentido.
questions.translation: Gracias por su tiempo y por las aportaciones útiles de hoy.

questions.question: You promise a written follow-up after the presentation. Which sentence is clearest?
options: I will send after the call one brief resume with the decisions and the actions agreed by us.
After the call, a short summary will be sent by me, where decisions and agreed actions are including.
I send a short summary after the call, included the decisions and accorded actions.
I'll send a short summary after the call, including the decisions and agreed actions.
questions.explanation: «I'll send...» expresa el compromiso futuro con claridad. «Including...» añade el contenido del resumen; «summary» no es «resume».
questions.translation: Enviaré un breve resumen después de la llamada, incluidas las decisiones y las acciones acordadas.
